summary: Kengo Harimoto is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Kyushu University and earned his PhD under Wilhelm Halbfass at the University of Pennsylvania. He has held positions at Mahidol University and the University of Naples "L'Orientale".

Kenichi Nakaya (1910–1987) was a historian who studied at the University of Tokyo from 1930 to 1933. He later served as a professor at the University of Tokyo from around 1955 to 1971 and taught at Seikei University from 1971 to 1981.

Kenji Kinugawa is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who studied at Kyoto University under Shigeru Shimizu, Hiroshi Kōzen, Ichiro Kominami, and Yoshitaka Iriya, as well as under Koichi Obi. He became an assistant professor at Hanazono University around 1991.
Kenji Matsuo is a historian and scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology. He studied at the University of Tokyo from 1974 to 1985 and held a post at Yamagata University from around 1987 to 2020.

Kenji Takahashi is an Indologist who studied at Leiden University and under supervisors including Diwakar Acharya, Yuko Yokochi, and Peter Bisschop. He completed a JSPS-sponsored fellowship at the University of Naples Federico II from 2019 to 2021.
Kenji Watanabe is an Indologist who studied under Jozef Deleu from around 1976 to 1979. He held an assistant post at Taisho University.
Kenjiu Kasawara (1851–1883) was a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Oxford from 1879 to 1883 under Friedrich Max Müller and Arthur Anthony Macdonell.

Kennard Lipman is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He completed his PhD at the University of Saskatchewan under Herbert V. Guenther and worked as a sessional instructor at the University of Calgary.

Kenneth Doo Young Lee is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology who studied at Columbia University under Ryuichi Abe and a committee including Robert A. F. Thurman. He held a post at Stetson University around 2004.

Kenneth G. Zysk is an Indologist and religious studies scholar. Educated at UC Santa Barbara and Australian National University, he held posts at Eastern Michigan University, the University of Copenhagen, the University of Wisconsin-Madison, the University of Toronto, and UCLA.

Kenneth J. Guest is a scholar of religious studies and Sinology. He studied at Columbia, Peking University, Union Theological Seminary, and CUNY, and later taught at Hunter College and Baruch College.

Kenneth J. Saunders (1883–1937) was a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies who studied under Wagiswara. He served as Professor of the History of Religion at Pacific School of Religion and as a lecturer at the University of California from 1921 to 1935.

Kenneth K. Inada (1923–2011) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He served as a professor at the University at Buffalo from around 1969 to 1997 and chaired the Numata Center for Buddhist Translation and Research from 1997 to 1999.

Kenneth K. Tanaka is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo and UC Berkeley under Padmanabh S. Jaini. He held positions at the Institute of Buddhist Studies, Musashino University, and Bukkyō Dendō Kyōkai.

Kenneth Roy Norman (1925–2020) was a scholar of Indology, linguistics, and Buddhist studies who studied at Downing College. He held posts at the University of Cambridge, the Pali Text Society as president, and SOAS as a visiting professor.

Kenryo Minowa is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo. He held posts at Rissho University, Eastern Institute, Aichi Gakuin University, Toyo University, and returned to the University of Tokyo as professor in 2010.
Kenryu Nishio is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who earned a doctorate in literature at Otani University. He served at Hanazono University, where he became professor emeritus around 2008.
Kenryu Tsuji (1919–2004) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ryukoku University from 1938 to 1941 and at the University of Toronto.

Kenryu Tsukinowa (1888–1969) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who studied at Bukkyo University. He was a professor at Ryukoku University from around 1928 to 1959 and taught at Bukkyo, Koyasan, and Shuchiin Universities.
Kenshi Kusano is a scholar of history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. He studied at Otani University from 1971 to 1980 and served as a professor there from around 1996 to 2018.
